      4.0.0: Architecture overhaul (breaking). Every calendar is composed from reusable holiday-definition classes (PublicHoliday.HolidayDefinitions: Christian/Common/Islamic/CountrySpecific); the calendar classes themselves stay in the root PublicHoliday namespace. Holiday names moved out of code into one embedded .resx per culture (Localization/Names), so a calendar answers in its own language and any caller can ask for another: Holiday.Name is the calendar's language, Holiday.EnglishName is always English, Holiday.GetName(culture) is a named language, and a name is never empty. Greece and the Quebec government calendar now name their holidays in Greek and French instead of English, and no longer depend on the ambient UI culture. Every calendar exposes a settable Culture (plus a WithCulture extension) so one app can follow the user's locale: PublicHolidayFactory.GetPublicHolidayForCountry(code).WithCulture(user). Translations you supply yourself can be registered through the new IHolidayNameProvider hook (HolidayNameProviders.Add, or ResourceManagerNameProvider over your own .resx). BREAKING: PublicHolidayNames returns IDictionary<DateTime, string[]> (one entry per holiday on a day - same-day holidays are no longer merged into one string or dropped); IHoliday.IdTextLocalization is renamed to HolidayKey and every key is a constant on the new HolidayKeys class (h.HolidayKey == HolidayKeys.Christmas - no more magic strings); IHoliday.GetName() with no arguments is removed, use EnglishName; IHoliday gains Name and IPublicHolidays gains Culture (implement them if you implement those interfaces); GetName("en") now returns the holiday's own EnglishName, which fixes Australian/Canadian/New Zealand Boxing Day answering "St Stephen's Day"; the localization ids of Boxing Day (BoxingDay), South Africa's Day of Goodwill (DayOfGoodwillZA) and Workers' Day (WorkersDayZA) changed; removed [Obsolete] members UseCachingHolidays, Belgium.PublicHolidayNamesFrench, CanadaQuebecGovClosingDay.PublicHolidayNamesCulture. Montenegro added to PublicHolidayFactory/PublicHolidayCountryCode ("ME"). Fixes: previously dropped same-day holidays restored (Serbia Easter in Labour-Day-collision years, Norway/Finland Ascension collisions, Italy Liberation Day on Easter days); PublicHolidaysInformation returns holiday names for every calendar (previously only calendars with a custom override); PublicHolidayNames no longer throws for Brazil (Good Friday on 21 April, e.g. 2000) and Germany (Ascension on 1 May, e.g. 2008); Serbia PublicHolidays uses Orthodox Easter to match PublicHolidayNames; UK IsBankHoliday derives from the holiday list (St Andrew's Day observed in December now recognized); GetName threw on net35/net40 (the embedded resource was read as a file path); stale results when a region/state property changes after a first call. Latvia (3.17) rebuilt on holiday definitions with the same dates: each transferred day off (pārceltā brīvdiena) is a holiday of its own with its own HolidayKey; same-day Mother's Day and Whit Sunday are two names instead of one joined string; added the 24 September 2018 Pope Francis visit holiday.
